content_units: You already have a credible pivot story:   6 years in store management + strong Excel + bilingual German/English   is highly relevant for analyst roles in retail, e-commerce, operations, supply chain, and customer analytics.

Your   EUR 45,000+ target in Berlin is realistic   for entry-level/junior analyst roles if you build a focused portfolio and position yourself toward   business-facing analytics   rather than pure technical data roles.

Month 1   Set your analyst foundation   Refresh Excel: PivotTables, XLOOKUP, Power Query basics; strengthen SQL SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY, CASE; learn core metrics: revenue, margin, conversion, basket size, stock turn   1-page learning tracker + 1 Excel dashboard

Month 2   Build analyst thinking   Practice business questions, KPI definitions, root-cause analysis; learn basic statistics: averages, distributions, correlation, sampling; start BI tool   KPI glossary + 1 mini retail analysis
Month 3   Learn Power BI or Tableau   Focus on Power BI first for business roles in Germany; build data model, relationships, DAX basics, charts, filters   Interactive BI dashboard project
Month 4   Add Python selectively   Learn only analyst-useful Python: pandas, cleaning, CSV/Excel loading, simple charts; avoid deep software topics   Jupyter notebook cleaning + analysis project

Month 5   Create portfolio around your background   Build 2 strong retail/ops projects and 1 broader project; write concise case-study pages with business impact   Portfolio with 3 publishable projects
Month 6   Job-market alignment   Rewrite CV for analyst roles; optimize LinkedIn; prepare STAR stories showing analytical impact from store management   Analyst CV + LinkedIn + story bank
Month 7   Start targeted applications   Apply to junior analyst, reporting, BI, and operations analytics roles; practice SQL and dashboard interviews weekly   20-30 quality applications
Month 8   Interview conversion   Mock interviews; case questions; explain projects clearly; practice salary and role-fit positioning   Interview-ready project walkthroughs
Month 9   Close the gap to offer level   Fill weak spots from interviews; deepen SQL/Power BI; continue applications and networking   Offer-ready profile for junior analyst roles
Skill Priorities for Berlin Entry-Level Roles
Option 1:   SQL + Power BI + Excel     Best ROI for fast transition into business analyst/data analyst roles   Most important stack
Option 2:   Excel + Retail KPI storytelling     Strong differentiator because it connects directly to your management background   Fastest way to sound job-relevant
Option 3:   Python for analysts     Helpful but should be secondary to SQL and BI in your case   Nice-to-have for Month 4+
Option 4:   Data modeling and dashboards     Critical for interviews because many junior roles ask for reporting examples   Portfolio booster
- You need to become comfortable with joins, aggregation, filtering, date logic, subqueries, CTE basics.
- Target: solve common analyst tasks without help.
- In Berlin, many junior roles expect dashboarding and reporting.
- Focus on data model basics, DAX measures, slicers, business visuals.
- Since you’re already strong, turn that into a selling point:
- Power Query, PivotTables, charting, error checks, scenario analysis.
- This is where you can beat more technical candidates.
- Learn to frame findings as: problem → analysis → recommendation → impact.
- Learn enough to clean data and automate simple analysis.
- Do not let Python delay your applications.
Because you want   EUR 45,000+   and have business experience, start with roles where domain knowledge matters.
Option 1:   Junior Data Analyst (Retail / E-commerce / Operations)     Best fit for your background and salary target   Highest priority
Option 2:   BI Analyst / Reporting Analyst     Strong if you build good Power BI dashboards   Good salary potential
Option 3:   Operations Analyst     Your store management background transfers very well to staffing, process, inventory, and performance analysis   Strong narrative fit
Option 4:   Supply Chain / Demand Planning Analyst     Good if you enjoy inventory, forecasting, and logistics metrics   Retail-adjacent path
Roles to target later, not first
- Product Analyst in highly technical product orgs
Portfolio Projects That Match Your Background
Build   3 strong projects  , not 10 weak ones.
- Analyze sales, footfall, conversion rate, average basket size, staffing efficiency, returns, and shrinkage.
- Show store-level, category-level, and weekly trend views.
- Include recommendations like staffing changes, low-performing category interventions, and promotion timing.
- Use SKU-level data to identify stockouts, overstock, dead stock, and reorder opportunities.
- Show ABC analysis, turnover, days of inventory, and missed-sales risk.
- This is highly relevant for retail and supply chain analyst roles.
- Explore campaign performance, repeat purchase, average order value, discount impact, and basket composition.
- Compare promoted vs non-promoted items and quantify margin trade-offs.
- Best if presented as a short business case study.
- A screenshot or live dashboard link if possible
- Weeks 25-36: applications + interview practice + improvement loop
- You already made business decisions using data in retail operations.
- You understand frontline operations, staffing, inventory, customer behavior, and KPI trade-offs.
- You are not a “career switcher from zero”; you are an   operations professional formalizing analytical skills  .
- Your bilingual German/English ability is a real advantage in Berlin teams.
Instead of only listing store duties, rewrite achievements into analyst language:
- Improved weekly sales tracking and reporting
- Monitored conversion, staffing efficiency, shrinkage, and stock availability
- Identified trends and supported actions to improve revenue or reduce waste
- Coordinated across teams using KPI-based decisions
Realistic Hiring Outlook and Salary Fit
- If a role is titled   intern  ,   working student  , or very junior startup analyst, it may fall below target.
- If you present 3 strong projects and interview well, a range around   EUR 45,000-52,000   is plausible in Berlin for the right junior/business-facing analyst role.
- Mid-size German companies needing reporting and KPI ownership
